question: Does the refreshed merge result preserve the shipped Node and Control UI authentication, reconnect, close, request-finalization, and browser-bundling contracts closely enough to make this shared lifecycle engine canonical?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well-proven, but it intentionally moves several security- and compatibility-sensitive invariants into one new owner boundary; accepting that boundary and its package export requires Gateway ownership judgment.

options.title: Approve after parity review
options.body: Rebase the branch and land it after a Gateway/client owner verifies the combined Node and browser lifecycle contracts against the exact merge result.

options.title: Pause the consolidation
options.body: Keep the two implementations until any remaining auth, reconnect, close-code, packaging, or public-surface ambiguity can be narrowed into smaller preparatory changes.

recommendation.title: Approve after parity review
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch and land it after a Gateway/client owner verifies the combined Node and browser lifecycle contracts against the exact merge result.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged SDK and net-policy history plus the trusted security-operations context make this the strongest available routing candidate for the final boundary decision.
